AcceptInvitation.description: A request to accept a link.

oneOf.description:
The account to make and let in, for a request without a session. A request with
a session lets in the account of the session, and names none.

language.description:
The language tag of the screen the request comes from (`ko`, `en-GB`): the
language of the mail that confirms a new account's address, where the server asks
for that (English, Korean); English for any other. A new account's welcome
board is written in it too, if it is English or Korean.

AcceptedInvitation.description: Where an accepted link let somebody in.

containerId.description: For a guest: the board or the wiki they were invited to.

oneOf.description: For a guest: which of the two it is, so that they are sent to its own address.

AccountChange.description: What a user changes of their name. A member that is left out stays as it is.

credentials.description:
The degrees and qualifications written after the name: at most three, each once,
in the order they are written. `null` or empty for none.

customName.description: The name the person wrote to be shown by; as `firstName`.

firstName.description:
The given name, in the letters the person writes it in: at most 64 UTF-16 code
units without control characters. Empty or `null` for none.

lastName.description: The family name, in the letters the person writes it in; as `firstName`.

latinFirstName.description: The given name in Latin letters; as `firstName`.

latinLastName.description: The family name in Latin letters; as `firstName`.

oneOf.description: Which name the person is shown by; `null` leaves it as it is.
The title written before the name; `null` for none.

AccountDeletion.description:
What deleting the account of the session comes to: what stands in its way, what
goes with it, and, once it was asked, until when it waits.

deleteAfter.description:
When the account is erased at the earliest, in milliseconds since the Unix
epoch; left out while the deletion is not asked.

graceDays.description: How many days an account waits between the asking and the erasing.

lastInstanceAdmin.description:
Whether the account is the server's only administrator, who stays: the server
keeps one.

organizations.description:
The organizations that have nobody but the account, which go with it, and
everything in them. The server's own first organization is never one.

proof.description: How the request shows that it is the person's.

requestedAt.description:
When the deletion was asked, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch; left out
while it is not.

soleAdminOf.description:
The organizations the account is the only administrator of that stay when it
goes: those that have other people in them, and the server's own first
organization, which goes with no account. Somebody else is made an
administrator of each before the account can be deleted.

AccountDeletionAsked.description: The answer to a request to delete the account.

deleteAfter.description:
When the account is erased at the earliest, in milliseconds since the Unix
epoch.

AdminChange.description: Whether a user is to be an administrator of the instance.

isAdmin.description: `true` makes the user an administrator, `false` ends that.

AuditAction.description: What a record of the audit log says was done.

AuditPerson.description: A user as a record of the audit log names them.

displayName.description: The name the user shows; empty for none.

username.description: The user's login name; empty if the account is gone.

AuditRecord.description: One record of the audit log: who did what, to what and whom, and when.

createAt.description: When, in milliseconds since the epoch.

detail.description:
The issuer a record of a provider's move names (`oidc_former_provider_…`,
`oidc_identity_…`); `null` for the others.

identity.description:
Who the identity a record of `oidc_identity_bound` or
`oidc_identity_carried_over` tied is: the email address its provider gave, or
its subject where it gave none, as it was then. `null` for the others, and in
the records of a workspace: the organization's are read by its administrators
alone.

oneOf.description: Whom it was done to, for an action that names somebody; `null` otherwise.

targetId.description: What it was done to: a board, a workspace or the organization.

targetName.description:
The name of the target, where the reader may know it: the title of a board
they see, the name of a workspace. `null` otherwise.

AuditRecordActor.description:
Who did what a record of the audit log says: a person by their account, named as it
is now (an account that is gone by its identifier alone), the server's operator,
who acts through the local administration socket without one, or the server
itself, for what its timers do. `kind` says which.

allOf.description: A person, whose identifier stays in the record when the account goes.

oneOf.description: A person, whose identifier stays in the record when the account goes.
The server's operator.
The server itself: what ends when its time runs out.

Block.description: The basic data unit of a board.

oneOf.description:
The body of a card, a comment or a page; `null` for a block without one. Only
those have one: a body on another block is refused (400 naming `body`). Every image of
it shows a file of the block's board. Whoever reads it by the board's link gets
every mention with an empty `userId`: a shape that is only sent, which a write
would have refused.

containerId.description: The identifier of the board the block belongs to.

createAt.description: Creation time in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

createdBy.description: The identifier of the user who created the block.

deleteAt.description: Deletion time in milliseconds since the Unix epoch; zero if not deleted.

editedAt.description:
For a comment whose body was changed: when that last happened, in milliseconds
since the Unix epoch. Absent for a comment never changed and for every other
block. The server sets it, and ignores a client's. What the body said before is
`getCommentVersions`'.

fields.description:
Type-specific data, free-form: serialized, at most 64,000 characters for a card, a
comment, an attachment or a page and 800,000 for a view or a block of another
type. The `icon` of a card is a string and its `isTemplate` a boolean, or either
`null` (400 naming `fields` otherwise). A page has its `icon` and its `order`
here, as `Page` gives them.

modifiedBy.description: The identifier of the user who last modified the block.

parentId.description: The identifier of the parent block; empty for root blocks.

schema.description: The schema version of the block.

title.description: The display title. A title with U+0000 is refused (400 naming `title`).

type.description:
The block type: `card`, `view`, `comment` or `attachment` on a board, and `page`
and `comment` (on a page) on a wiki. No request of blocks makes a block of
another type or patches one into it (400 naming `type`), nor a page:
`createPage` makes those, and `createPageComment` the comments of a wiki.

updateAt.description: Last modification time in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

BlockPatch.description: A partial update of a `Block`. Absent members leave the block unchanged.

oneOf.description:
The new body of a card or a comment; `null` takes the body away. Sent only with
`readAt` (400 naming `readAt` without it).

readAt.description:
The `updateAt` of the block as the client read it. If the block has changed
since, the patch is refused.

type.description:
The new block type: `card`, `view`, `comment` or `attachment`. Any other is
refused (400 naming `type`).

updatedFields.description: Fields to set, replacing any existing value under the same key.

BlockPatchBatch.description: A batch of block identifiers and the patch to apply to each, matched by position.

blockIds.description: The identifiers of the blocks to patch.

Body.description: A document of the editor: a node of type `doc` whose `content` is its blocks. Which nodes, marks and attributes it may have, and how they nest, is the allowlist of `docs/s6-design.md` 5.7. At most 1 MiB as JSON, 32 levels deep and 20,000 nodes.

BodyVersion.description:
A version kept of a card's body: the body as it was at a time, and who wrote it up
to then.

editors.description:
Who wrote the body up to this version since the one before, in the order of
their identifiers: those who edited it and those who wrote it whole. Empty for
a body nobody is known to have written.

isCurrent.description:
Whether the body of this version is the one the card has now. Of versions
with the same body, the newest; of none while the card's editors have typed
what is not written to the card yet.

keptAt.description:
When the version was kept, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch. For a body
nobody is known to have written (one from before versions were kept, or from an
import), when the card was last changed.

version.description:
The place of the version among the card's, counted from 1. The server keeps the
newest ones: the lowest numbers go as new versions come.

BodyVersionContent.description: A version kept of a card's body, with the body.

oneOf.description: The body of the card then; `null` if it had none.

editors.description:
Who wrote the body up to this version since the one before, in the order of
their identifiers. Empty for a body nobody is known to have written.

isCurrent.description:
Whether the body of this version is the one the card has now. Of versions
with the same body, the newest; of none while the card's editors have typed
what is not written to the card yet.

keptAt.description: When the version was kept, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

version.description: The place of the version among the card's, counted from 1.

Card.description: A card: a titled group of properties with a body on a board.

boardId.description: The identifier of the board the card belongs to.

oneOf.description:
The card's body. `null` for a card without one, and in a list of cards, which
says only whether there is one (`hasBody`): a card is read alone for its body.

createAt.description: Creation time in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

createdBy.description: The identifier of the user who created the card.

deleteAt.description: Deletion time in milliseconds since the Unix epoch; zero if not deleted.

hasBody.description: Whether the card has a body.

icon.description: The card's icon; at most one grapheme.

isTemplate.description: Whether the card is a template.

lastCommentAt.description:
When the card's last comment was posted (the `createAt` of the newest of its
comments, the blocks of the type `comment` directly on it), in milliseconds since
the Unix epoch; zero if it has none. Changing a comment does not change it; a
deleted comment does not count, and counts again with its time if restored. A
comment does not change the card's `updateAt`. A new comment comes as
`UPDATE_BLOCK`, so a client can keep the newer time; after a deletion the card is
read again for it. A number sent here in a request is ignored.

modifiedBy.description: The identifier of the user who last modified the card.

oneOf.description:
What a gallery shows of the card's body: only in a list asked for it
(`getCards` with `preview=true`), and left out otherwise. A request need not send
it; what it sends is not stored.

properties.description:
Property values keyed by property identifier: a string, a list of strings, or
`null`, and for a property of the type `date` a date value (`{"from":
"2026-03-05"}`, `{"from": "2026-03-05", "to": "2026-03-09"}` or `{"from":
1772703000000}`) or `null`.

tasksDone.description: How many task items of the body are checked.

tasksTotal.description: How many task items the body has.

updateAt.description: Last modification time in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

CardPatch.description: What a card is changed to. A member that is left out stays as it is.

oneOf.description: The new body; `null` takes the body away. Sent only with `readAt`.

deletedProperties.description:
Identifiers of properties whose value the card is to lose. A property named here
and in `updatedProperties` loses its value.

icon.description: The new icon; at most one grapheme.

readAt.description:
The `updateAt` of the card as the client read it: if the card has changed since,
the patch is refused with 409 and changes nothing. Needed with `body`, and
checked whenever it is sent.

updatedProperties.description:
Property values to set, by property identifier, each replacing the card's value
for that property. The card's other values stay as they are: two patches that
set different properties of a card at about the same time both keep theirs, and
of two that set the same property the later one wins.

CardPreview.description: What a gallery shows of a card's body.

imageFileId.description:
The file the body's first image shows (`getFile` gives it, and `getSharedFile` to
the holder of the board's link); empty if the body has no image.

text.description:
The beginning of the body's text: its plain text as it is searched (a line per
paragraph, heading, code block and formula block, separated by `\n`; a formula
gives its source, an image and a mention nothing), at most 200 UTF-16 code units,
cut between characters as they are seen (a flag or a letter with its accent stays
whole), without white space at its end. Nothing says it was cut. Empty for a card
without text.

Category.description: A sidebar category of one user in one workspace.

collapsed.description: Whether the category is collapsed in the sidebar.

createAt.description: Creation time in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

deleteAt.description: Deletion time in milliseconds since the Unix epoch; zero if not deleted.

sortOrder.description: The position of the category among the user's categories.

type.description: Whether this is a system or a custom category.

updateAt.description: Last modification time in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

userId.description: The identifier of the user the category belongs to.

workspaceId.description: The identifier of the workspace the category belongs to.

CategoryContainerMetadata.description: A board's place in a category.

hidden.description: Whether the user has hidden the board from the sidebar.

allOf.description: The category. Its members appear inline in the JSON form.

CategoryContainers.description: A category together with the boards in it, in display order.

CategoryType.description: Whether a category was created by the server or by the user.

CategoryUpdate.description:
What a sidebar category is changed to. The name and the collapsed state are what
changes; a system category keeps its name.

collapsed.description: Whether the category is collapsed in the sidebar. Left out, it is not.

ChangePasswordRequest.description: A request to change a user's password.

ClientConfig.description: The part of the server configuration that the web client needs.

allowPublicLinks.description:
Whether boards and wikis may be shared publicly through a read token: the
setting `allow_public_links`.

maxFileBytes.description:
The largest upload the server accepts, in bytes; always more than zero (100 MiB
unless the server is configured otherwise): the setting `max_file_bytes`.

maxImportBytes.description:
The largest archive an import takes, in bytes; always more than zero (256 MiB
unless the server is configured otherwise): the setting `max_import_bytes`.

nameDisplay.description: How other users' names are displayed: the setting `name_display`.

searchEnabled.description:
Whether what cards and pages say can be searched (`searchWorkspaceContent`):
always, on this server. It searches its search server, or its database where none
is configured; a search server that does not answer, or cannot hold the index,
answers each search 503 (`search_unavailable`).

CommentVersion.description:
A text a comment had before its body was changed: the body then, who wrote it and
when. The first is the comment as it was posted.

oneOf.description: The body of the comment then; `null` if it had none.

version.description:
The place of the version among the comment's, counted from 1 for the text it was
posted with. Versions the server no longer keeps leave gaps.

writtenAt.description: When this version was written, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

writtenBy.description:
Who wrote this version: the author of the comment for the first one, and for
each later one who changed the body to it.

password.description:
The password the registration was made with: needed where the link is opened in
another browser than the one the registration was made from, and not read in
that one.

token.description: The secret from the confirmation link's fragment.

Container.description: A board: a set of blocks and the property definitions of its cards.

cardProperties.description: The property definitions of the board's cards, in display order.

createAt.description: Creation time in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

createdBy.description:
The identifier of the user who created the board; empty for a built-in template,
which no user made.

deleteAt.description: Deletion time in milliseconds since the Unix epoch; zero if not deleted.

icon.description: The board's icon, usually one emoji.

isBuiltin.description:
Whether the board is one of the templates the server ships with. They are
offered to every workspace and nobody can change them. The server decides this:
what a client sends here is ignored.

isTemplate.description: Whether the board is a template.

kind.description:
What the board is for: `board` for cards, `wiki` for pages. It is what the board
was made as and never changes; a board decoded without it is a `board`. A wiki
is no template and has no card properties, and the operations that are about
cards answer for a wiki as for a board that is not there.

minimumRole.description:
The role a user gets who joins the board, or is added by somebody who does not
manage its roles. Never empty and never admin.

modifiedBy.description: The identifier of the user who last modified the board.

properties.description: Free-form properties of the board itself.

showDescription.description: Whether the description is shown in the interface.

templateVersion.description: The version of the built-in template this board came from.

title.description:
The board's title. No text of a board (this, `description`, `icon`, and the
strings and member names of `properties` and `cardProperties`) holds U+0000:
400 naming the member.

type.description: Whether the board is open or private.

updateAt.description: Last modification time in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

workspaceId.description: The identifier of the workspace the board belongs to.

ContainerKind.description:
What a container of a workspace is for: a board holds cards and their views, a wiki
holds pages. A container is of one kind from when it is made and never of another.

ContainerMember.description: A user's membership of a board.

oneOf.description: The highest role inherited from teams; direct flags remain unchanged.

schemeCommenter.description: The user may comment on the board's cards.

schemeEditor.description: The user may edit the board.

schemeViewer.description: The user may view the board.

synthetic.description: The membership has no directly stored role record.

ContainerPatch.description: A partial update of a `Container`. Absent members leave the board unchanged.

deletedCardProperties.description: Identifiers of card property definitions to remove.

deletedProperties.description: Keys of board properties to remove.

oneOf.description: The new minimum role.
The new board type.

updatedCardProperties.description: Card property definitions to add or replace, matched by their `id`.

ContainerTeam.description: A workspace team and the role its members inherit on a board.

role.description: No team may administer a board.

team.description: The group, including its current nonguest members.

ContainerTeamRole.description: The role given to a team on a board.

role.description: The team's role, at most editor.

ContainerType.description: Who may see and join a board.

ContainersAndBlocks.description: Boards and the blocks that belong to them, created together.

blocks.description: The blocks; each must belong to one of `containers`.

Credential.description: A degree or a professional qualification written after a person's name.

DeleteAccountRequest.description: A request to delete the account of the session.

password.description:
The account's password; left out, or empty, by an account that has none. Not
`null`, as no member that is not optional is.

username.description: The account's login name, typed out: that the person means this account.

DeleteContainersAndBlocks.description: The identifiers of boards and blocks to delete together.

DeletedItem.description:
A card or a board in the trash, with as much as it takes to decide whether to bring
it back (`undeleteBlock`, `undeleteContainer`).

deletedAt.description: When it was deleted, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

deletedBy.description: The identifier of who deleted it, who may no longer exist; empty if not known.

id.description: The identifier of the card or the board.

oneOf.description:
For a board, its kind: the trash of boards lists boards and wikis together. Left
out for a card.

title.description: Its title when it was deleted.

DeletedPage.description:
A page in the trash, at the top of what went with it, as the trash of a wiki lists
it: `undeletePage` brings it back with the pages below it.

below.description: How many pages below it went with it, and come back with it.

deletedAt.description: When it was deleted, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

deletedBy.description: Who deleted it, who may no longer exist; empty if not known.

icon.description: The page's icon when it was deleted; empty for none.

parentId.description:
The page it was below; empty for one at the top of the wiki. It may be gone: the
page then comes back at the top.

title.description: The page's title when it was deleted.

DeletionProof.description: How an account shows that the request to delete it is its person's.

Density.description: How much room the interface gives each thing.

EmailVerified.description: Where a confirmed registration's account was let in.

containerId.description: For a guest's link: the board or the wiki it was let onto.

oneOf.description:
For a guest's link: which of the two it is, so that they are sent to its own
address.

organizationStarted.description:
Whether the registration started its organization, rather than joining one by
the link of an invitation.

workspaceId.description:
The workspace: the first of the organization it started, or the one its link
leads into.

file.description:
The file. An upload needs the part to have a file name; an archive to import
does not.

FileInfo.description: What the server records about an uploaded file.

createAt.description: Creation time in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

extension.description: The lower-cased extension of the name, with its leading dot.

name.description: The name the file was uploaded under.

size.description: The size of the file in bytes.

password.description: The new password: at least eight characters, at most 1024 bytes.

token.description: The secret from the reset link's fragment.

GuestInvitationsChange.description: A request to turn the invitations of guests to a workspace's boards on or off.

enabled.description: Whether the admins of the workspace's boards may invite guests to them.

HourCycle.description: How the hours of a day are written. The names are those of the browsers' `Intl`.

ImportRequest.description: An archive to import: one sent in parts with `createImportUpload`.

uploadId.description:
The upload of the archive, every part of it received. It is thrown away by the
import, whether the import succeeds or not.

ImportResult.description: What an import did beyond making the archive's boards.

membersLeftOut.description:
How many of the users who were members of the archive's boards were left out of
the boards made of them, because they are not in the workspace; each counted
once. Who they are is not told.

InvalidInput.description:
One thing of a request that was refused, and where in the request it is: exactly
one of `pointer`, `parameter` and `header` says.

detail.description: What is wrong with it, in English. Not for showing to users.

header.description: The name of the request header.

parameter.description:
The name of the parameter of the query or of the path, or of the part of a
multipart form.

pointer.description:
A JSON Pointer (RFC 6901) to the member of the request body: `/username`,
`/blockPatches/2/title`.

reason.description:
Why it was refused, stable: the `reason` of the problem where it has one, else
what the check found: `required` (missing or blank), `too_short`, `too_long`,
`invalid_format` (not the form the member has), `invalid_characters`, `unknown`
(the request has no such member), or `invalid` where no finer cause is told.

Invitation.description: A link that lets somebody into a workspace.

containerId.description: For a guest: the board or the wiki they are invited to.

containerRole.description: For a guest: their role on that board, `viewer`, `commenter` or `editor`.

createAt.description: When the link was made, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

createdBy.description: The identifier of the user who made the link.

expiresAt.description: When the link stops letting anybody in, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

id.description: The invitation's identifier, by which it is revoked. It lets nobody in.

maxUses.description:
How often the link may be used; left out for one that is used as often as it is
until it ends.

parentId.description:
For a guest link made for one recipient of a mailed guest link: the link it was
made like. Revoking that one revokes this one while nobody used it.

recipient.description: For such a link: the address it was mailed to.

role.description: What whoever accepts becomes in the workspace: `member`, or `guest`.

token.description: The token of the link: in the answer that makes the link, and in no other.

uses.description: How often the link was used.

workspaceId.description: The workspace the link leads into.

InvitationMail.description: A request to email an existing invitation to one or more recipients.

language.description:
The sender's screen language, used for a recipient when neither the recipient's
nor the sender's setting names a language the mail is written in.

recipients.description: Email addresses, each delivered separately; duplicates are sent once.

token.description: The secret of the existing invitation, sent only in the request body.

InvitationPreview.description: What a link shows of where it leads, to whoever holds it.

oneOf.description: For a guest: which of the two it is.

containerTitle.description: For a guest: the title of the board or the wiki they are invited to.

inviterName.description:
The name of who made the link: the name they are shown by, or their login name
if they have none.

workspaceName.description: The name of the workspace the link leads into; empty if it was given none.

InvitationToken.description: A request that carries the token of a link and nothing else.

LeavingOrganization.description:
An organization that goes with the account of its only member, and how much is in
it. The numbers are left out for an organization the session that asks does not
open (one that takes only sessions made through its provider).

boards.description: How many boards it has in use, templates not counted.

files.description: How many files its boards and wikis in use hold.

name.description: Its name; empty if it was given none.

wikis.description: How many wikis it has in use.

LinkedBlock.description: A card or a page as a reference shows it: what it is called, and where it is.

containerId.description: The identifier of the board the card is on, or of the wiki the page is of.

containerKind.description: Whether that is a board or a wiki.

icon.description: Its icon, at most one grapheme; empty for none.

id.description: The identifier of the card or the page.

kind.description: Whether it is a card or a page.

title.description: Its title; empty for one without.

LinkedIdentity.description:
An identity tied to an account: who its owner is at a provider, by which they sign
in to it through the provider of an organization.

createAt.description: When it was tied, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

email.description:
The email address the provider gave when the identity was tied: its word,
checked by nobody. Empty if it gave none.

issuer.description: The issuer, as the provider names itself.

madeThisSession.description:
Whether the session that asks was made for this identity, or through a provider
of its issuer before sessions knew their subject: removing the identity ends
that session too.

subject.description: Who the account's owner is at the issuer.

LinkedKind.description: What a reference may name: a card of a board or a page of a wiki.

LoginOptions.description: What the login page shows: the organization it is for, if it is for one.

emailVerification.description:
Whether a registration opens nothing until the link mailed to its address
confirms it, which signs it in (`email_verification`).

mailEnabled.description: Whether this server can deliver password recovery and invitation mail.

oneOf.description:
The organization the page is for: the one named, or the only one of a server
that holds one. `null` for none, also for an identifier that names none.

registrationOpen.description:
Whether somebody without an invitation may register and start an organization: on a
server where everybody may, and on any server until its first user did. Where it
is `false`, the link of an invitation is the way in.

LoginOrganization.description: What the login page may know of an organization before anybody signs in.

id.description: The organization's identifier, for starting a sign-in through its provider.

name.description: The organization's name; empty if it was given none.

oidc.description: Whether signing in through the organization's provider is on.

email.description: The email address to log in with, used when no user has the given name.

username.description: The user name to log in with.

MemberRoles.description:
The roles a member of a board is to have. A role that is left out is taken away, and
a member with no role may do nothing on the board, not even view it.

schemeCommenter.description: The user may comment on the board's cards.

schemeEditor.description: The user may edit the board.

schemeViewer.description: The user may view the board.

MinimumRole.description:
The minimum role of a board: the role a user gets who joins the board, or is added
to it by somebody who does not manage its roles.

A board always has one, and it is never admin: nobody becomes an administrator of a
board by joining it.

NameShown.description:
Which name a person is shown by. When it is empty the next one down the list is
taken; the login name is the last.

NewAccount.description:
The account somebody asks for: who registers, and who accepts an invitation
without having one.

displayName.description:
The name to be shown by; may be left out or empty for none, not `null`. Checked
as `patchMe` checks it: at most 64 UTF-16 code units without control characters.

containerId.description:
The board the block belongs to: the board of the path, or, where boards and
blocks are made together, the `id` of one of the request's boards.

createAt.description:
Must be 1 or more. The server does not keep it: the block is created when the
server stores it.

fields.description:
Type-specific data, free-form: serialized, at most 64,000 characters for a card,
a comment or an attachment and 800,000 for a view. The `properties` of a card
among them are values by property identifier: a string, a list of strings, or
`null`.

id.description:
A name for the block within the request. The server gives every block a new
identifier, and where one block of the request names another (as its `parentId`,
or in the fields `contentOrder`, `cardOrder` and `defaultTemplateId`) it puts
the new identifier there. Blocks that come under one name get one identifier,
which cannot be stored twice; a block that no other names needs no `id`.

parentId.description:
The block this one is below: a block of the same board, or the name of another
block of the request. Left out for a block directly on its board.

schema.description: The schema version of the block.

type.description:
The block type: `card`, `view`, `comment` or `attachment`. Any other type is
refused (400 naming `type`): a card's content is its body.

updateAt.description: Must be 1 or more. The server does not keep it.

cardProperties.description:
The property definitions of the board's cards, in display order. Each needs a
non-empty `id` that no other has.

icon.description: The board's icon, usually one emoji.

id.description:
Only where boards and blocks are made together, and needed there: a name by
which the blocks of the request say which board they belong to. The server gives
the board another identifier. Where one board is made, a board with an `id` is
refused.

isTemplate.description: Whether the board is a template.

minimumRole.description: The role a user gets who joins the board. Left out, `editor`.

properties.description: Free-form properties of the board itself.

showDescription.description: Whether the description is shown in the interface.

templateVersion.description: The version of the built-in template the board came from.

type.description: Whether the board is open or private.

boardId.description: The board of the path, if it is there at all.

oneOf.description: The card's body; left out or `null` for none.

icon.description: The card's icon; at most one grapheme.

isTemplate.description: Whether the card is a template.

properties.description: Property values by property identifier: a string, a list of strings, or `null`.

collapsed.description: Whether the category is collapsed in the sidebar.

sortOrder.description:
The position of the category among the user's categories. It is stored 10
higher: see `createCategory`.

type.description:
Left out, `custom`. A category that is made as `system` can be neither renamed
nor deleted afterwards.

userId.description: The user of the session: a user makes categories for themselves only.

NewContainersAndBlocks.description: Boards and their blocks, to make together.

blocks.description: The blocks, at least one. The `containerId` of each is the `id` of one of `containers`.

containers.description: The boards, at least one. Each needs an `id`.

NewInvitation.description: A request to make a link.

containerId.description: For a guest: the board or the wiki they are invited to. Not for a member.

containerRole.description:
For a guest: their role on that board, `viewer`, `commenter` or `editor`; an
editor if left out. Not for a member.

role.description: What whoever accepts becomes in the workspace: `member`, or `guest`.

NewMember.description:
A user to make a member of a board, and the roles to give them. A member with no
role may do nothing on the board, not even view it.

schemeAdmin.description:
The user administers the board. Only who manages the board's roles may ask for
this.

schemeCommenter.description: The user may comment on the board's cards.

schemeEditor.description: The user may edit the board.

schemeViewer.description: The user may view the board.

userId.description: The identifier of the user, who must be able to see the board's workspace.

after.description:
The identifier of the page it goes right after: a page of the same parent. Empty
for the first place; left out or `null`, the last place.

icon.description: The page's icon, at most one grapheme. Left out, none.

parentId.description:
The identifier of the page it goes below: a page of the same wiki. Left out or
empty, the page is at the top of the wiki.

title.description: The page's title. Left out, empty.

NewPageComment.description: A comment to write on a page.

body.description: The comment's text, as a page's body is written; neither empty nor `null`.

blockId.description: The identifier of the block subscribed to.

blockType.description: The type of the block subscribed to.

subscriberId.description: The user of the session: a user subscribes for themselves only.

NewUpload.description: A file to send in parts.

contentType.description:
The content type of the file, at most 255 characters. The server does not go by
it: what a file is served as follows from its name.

name.description:
The name of the file, as `uploadFile` takes one: 1 to 255 characters, without
U+0000, of which what follows its last `/` is kept. A name whose last segment,
parted by `/` or `\`, is blank (`dir/`), `.` or `..` is refused. The stored file
keeps its extension, as `uploadFile` keeps it.

size.description:
The size of the file in bytes. More than `maxFileBytes` of `getClientConfig` is
413 (`file_too_large`).

description.description: The wiki's description. Left out, empty.

icon.description: The wiki's icon, usually one emoji. Left out, none.

minimumRole.description: The role a user gets who joins the wiki. Left out, `editor`.

title.description: The wiki's title. Left out, empty.

type.description:
Whether the wiki is open (`O`), for whoever works in the workspace to read, and to
join to write in it, or private (`P`), for whom it is shared with.

OidcFormerProvider.description:
The provider an organization moved away from, kept for a while: nobody signs in
through it, but somebody the new provider vouches for who has no account yet may
show who they were at it, and so tie the new identity to the account they had.

createAt.description: When the organization moved away from it, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

expiresAt.description: When it is kept no longer, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

OidcFormerProviderEnd.description: Which former provider an administrator ends the keeping of: the one they read.

createAt.description: The `createAt` of the former provider as it was read.

OidcPendingProvider.description:
The pending settings of an organization's provider, without the client secret:
`hasClientSecret` says whether there is one.

bindsIdentityUntil.description:
Until when a trial from the session that asks, come back by then, ties an
identity of another issuer that is nobody's yet to the administrator's own
account, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch: five minutes after the session
was made through the provider as it is stored. `null` once that has passed,
for a session that was not made so, and for pending settings of the same
issuer, which tie nothing.

createAt.description: When they were saved, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

hasClientSecret.description: Whether a client secret is saved with them.

OidcProvider.description:
The provider of an organization, as its administrators read it. The client secret
is not in it: only whether there is one.

autoJoin.description:
Whether somebody the provider vouches for who has no place in the organization
(no member of it, nor a guest of one of its workspaces) becomes a member of it,
and of its default workspace, by signing in. A guest signs in as a guest.

canRequireSso.description:
Whether this session was made through this provider, switched on, as it is
stored now: a change of the issuer, the client, the secret or the switch since
asks for signing in through it again before `ssoRequired` is switched on.

clientId.description: The client identifier the provider gave this server.

createAt.description: When the provider was first set, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

enabled.description: Whether signing in through the provider is on.

oneOf.description:
The provider the organization signed in through before its issuer changed,
while it is kept for its people to carry their accounts over; `null` for none.

hasClientSecret.description: Whether a client secret is stored.

issuer.description: The issuer: an `https` address, exactly as the provider names itself.

oneOf.description:
The settings saved aside while the organization takes no password, which
nobody signs in through until a sign-in through them ends well; `null` for
none.

redirectUri.description:
The address the provider sends people back to, to be registered with it exactly:
the organization's own, which does not change with the provider.

ssoRequired.description:
Whether the organization takes no password: what is the organization's opens
only for a session made through this provider.

updateAt.description: When the provider was last changed, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

OidcProviderSettings.description: What an administrator sets of the organization's provider.

autoJoin.description:
Whether somebody the provider vouches for who is no member becomes one. Left
out, it stays as it is; on when the organization has no provider.

clientId.description: The client identifier the provider gave this server.

clientSecret.description:
The client secret. Left out, the stored one stays while the issuer and the client
stay the same (none for a new provider), and is required with another issuer or
client when one is stored; the empty string stores none.

enabled.description:
Whether signing in through the provider is on. Left out, it stays as it is; on
when the organization has no provider.

issuer.description: The issuer: an `https` address without query or fragment.

ssoRequired.description:
Whether the organization takes no password. Left out, it stays as it is; off
when the organization has no provider.

OidcStart.description: A sign-in through a provider that was started: where the page sends the browser.

authorizationUrl.description: The provider's address that asks the person to sign in, for this sign-in.

OidcStartRequest.description: What a sign-in through a provider is started with. Nothing, to sign in.

linkPassword.description:
The password of the account of the request's session. With it the sign-in
links: what the provider vouches for is tied to that account, in place of
signing in.

allOf.description:
The parts of the user's name, and their title and credentials: the
administrators see the user's name.

displayName.description: The name the user shows; empty for none.

role.description: What the user is in the organization.

OrgMember.description: A member of an organization, as its administrators list them.

OrgRole.description: What a member of an organization is in it.

OrgRoleChange.description: The role a member of an organization is given: the body of a change of it.

OrgWorkspace.description:
A workspace of an organization as its administrators list it: whether or not they
are in it, and whether or not it is in the trash. Nothing of what is in it.

deletedAt.description:
When it was put in the trash, in milliseconds since the epoch; zero while it is
in use.

isDefault.description: Whether it is the organization's default workspace, which cannot be deleted.

joinedAsOrgAdmin.description:
Whether the administrator who asks is in it as the organization's administrator,
having joined it as one: leaving gives back what they were before.

memberCount.description: How many members it has, its guests among them.

name.description: The workspace's name; empty if it was given none.

oneOf.description: What the administrator who asks is in it; `null` for no member.

Organization.description: An organization as its administrators see it.

defaultWorkspaceId.description:
The workspace somebody who joins the organization gets into. It cannot be
deleted.

name.description: The organization's name; empty if it was given none.

publicLinks.description:
Whether its boards may be read by a public link. Off, every link is closed and
none is made; on again, the links made before open again.

OrganizationName.description: An organization named to its member.

name.description: Its name; empty if it was given none.

OrganizationPatch.description: A change of an organization: what is left out stays as it is.

name.description: The new name, at most `MAX_NAME_CHARS` characters; may be empty.

publicLinks.description: Whether boards may be read by a public link.

oneOf.description: The page's body; `null` for a page without one.

createAt.description: Creation time in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

createdBy.description: The identifier of the user who made the page.

icon.description: The page's icon, at most one grapheme; empty for none.

modifiedBy.description: The identifier of the user who last changed the page.

order.description:
The page's place among the pages of the same parent, as in the tree
(`getPageTree`).

parentId.description: The identifier of the page it is below; empty for a page at the top of its wiki.

updateAt.description:
Last modification time in milliseconds since the Unix epoch: what `readAt` of a
change of the page names.

wikiId.description: The identifier of the wiki the page is of.

PageCommentPatch.description:
What a comment on a page is changed to: its text, written over the comment as it was
read.

body.description: The comment's new text, as a page's body is written; neither empty nor `null`.

readAt.description:
The `updateAt` of the comment as the client read it: if the comment has changed
since, the patch is refused with 409 and changes nothing.

PageDuplicate.description:
What a copy of a page, with every page below it, is given: its title, for the copy
of the page asked for alone (the pages below it keep theirs).

title.description:
The copy's title; left out or `null`, the page's own. A client names the copy
in its reader's language (" (copy)"): the server does not.

PageMove.description: Where a page moves to, with every page below it: within its wiki.

after.description:
The identifier of the page it goes right after: another page of that parent.
Empty for the first place; left out or `null`, the last place.

parentId.description:
The identifier of the page it goes below: a page of the same wiki, neither the
page itself nor one below it. Left out or empty, the page goes to the top of the
wiki.

PageNode.description: A page as the tree of its wiki lists it: without its body.

createAt.description: Creation time in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

icon.description: The page's icon, at most one grapheme; empty for none.

order.description:
The page's place among the pages of the same parent: they are listed by it as
strings compare (by code unit, not by a locale), and by `id` where two have the
same. The server makes it; a client reads it only to sort.

parentId.description: The identifier of the page it is below; empty for a page at the top of its wiki.

updateAt.description: Last modification time in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

PagePatch.description:
What a page is changed to. A member that is left out stays as it is. Where the page
is in the tree is none of them: a member the patch does not have is refused, so
that a request to move the page does not pass for one that did.

oneOf.description: The new body; `null` takes the body away. Sent only with `readAt`.

icon.description: The new icon, at most one grapheme; empty for none.

readAt.description:
The `updateAt` of the page as the client read it: if the page has changed since,
the patch is refused with 409 and changes nothing. Needed with `body`, and
checked whenever it is sent.

PatchContainersAndBlocks.description:
Patches for several boards and blocks, applied together.

Identifiers and patches are matched by position.

blockIds.description: The identifiers of the blocks to patch.

blockPatches.description: The block patches, one per block identifier.

containerIds.description: The identifiers of the boards to patch.

containerPatches.description: The board patches, one per board identifier.

PersonName.description: A person's name, every part of which may be empty.

credentials.description:
The degrees and qualifications written after the name, in the person's order: at
most three, each once.

customName.description: The name the person wrote to be shown by.

firstName.description: The given name, in the letters the person writes it in.

lastName.description: The family name, in the letters the person writes it in.

latinFirstName.description: The given name in Latin letters.

latinLastName.description: The family name in Latin letters.

nameShown.description: Which name the person is shown by.

oneOf.description: The title written before the name; `null` for none.

Problem.description:
The JSON body the server sends with every error status of the API, as
`application/problem+json` (RFC 9457).

A client decides by `status` and, where there is one, `reason`; both are stable,
and so is `type`. `title` and `detail` are English text for logs and developers.

detail.description:
What went wrong this time, in English. Not for showing to users, and without
internals.

errors.description:
What of the request was refused, one entry for each. `register`,
`changePassword`, `patchMe`, `patchUserSettings`, `patchClientState`,
`createSubscription`, `createUpload`, `createImportUpload`, `setSharing`,
`getCards`, `createCard` and `patchCard` list everything their check of the
request's own shape refuses, the first 100; so does the check of a category's
own members. Every other refusal names the one thing it is about: what is only
known from what is stored, a block of a request with several, and the first
node of a document (`body`) that may not be stored.

instance.description: The request this answer is to: `urn:uuid:` and the `requestId`.

orgId.description:
The organization whose provider the session must be made through, with the
reason `sso_required`: what the sign-in is started for. With the reason
`last_org_admin`, the organization that would be left without an administrator.

reason.description:
Why, where a client must tell causes of the same status apart, such as
`invalid_credentials` or `last_admin`.

requestId.description:
The identifier of the request, the same as in the `x-request-id` response header
and in the server's request log.

retryAfter.description: How many seconds to wait before trying again, as in the `Retry-After` header.

status.description: The HTTP status of the answer.

title.description: The name of the `type`, in English; the same for every problem of the type.

type.description:
What kind of problem this is: `/problems/<name>` under the path the server is
served at, the address of a page of text where the server describes the kind.
The same kind of problem has the same `type` every time. The name is that of the
`reason` where there is one, else that of the status, written with hyphens:
`/problems/last-admin`, `/problems/not-found`.

Readiness.description: The checks of the readiness: what the server depends on to serve.

database.description:
Whether the database reads the table of the sessions (it answers, and has not
lost a table every signed-in request reads), and this process holds the lock of
the server of the database in it.

files.description:
Whether the file storage can be used: a small file is written to it, read back and
removed, on the local disk as on the object store.

ReadinessCheck.description:
How one check came out. Its words are the whole answer: no cause of a failure
leaves the server, the log has it.

number.description: The number of the part, from 1.

ReferenceIds.description: The identifiers the references name, each the `id` of a node `reference`: at most 100.

RegisterRequest.description: A request to register a new user.

displayName.description:
The name to be shown by; may be left out or empty for none, not `null`. Checked
as `patchMe` checks it: at most 64 UTF-16 code units without control characters.

language.description:
The language tag of the screen the request comes from (`ko`, `en-GB`): the
language of the mail that confirms the address, where the server asks for that
(English, Korean); English for any other.

organizationName.description:
The name of the organization the account starts, and of that organization's
first workspace. Read as `organization_name` reads it.

email.description:
The address the registration was made with, used when no registration has the
given name.

language.description:
The requester's language tag (`ko`, `en-GB`), used when the registration's own
screen named no language the mail is written in (English, Korean); English if
neither does.

username.description:
The user name the registration was made with; or leave it empty and give the
address.

language.description:
The requester's language tag (`ko`, `en-GB`), used when the account's own setting
names no language the mail is written in (English, Korean); English if neither does.

SearchHit.description: One thing a search found: the user reads it now.

containerId.description: The identifier of the board the card is on, or of the wiki the page is in.

containerKind.description: What its container is: a board, or a wiki.

id.description: The identifier of the card or the page.

snippet.description:
A piece of its body around what matched, in stretches that follow one
another; empty where the body has changed since it was indexed, or has nothing
to show.

title.description: Its title as it is now.

SearchKind.description: The kind of thing a search finds.

build_date.description: The build date; empty unless set at build time.

build_number.description: The build number; empty unless set at build time.

commit.description: The commit the server was built from; empty unless set at build time.

os_arch.description: The CPU architecture the server runs on, as Rust names it (`x86_64`, `aarch64`).

os_type.description:
The operating system the server runs on, as Rust names it (`linux`, `macos`,
`windows`).

version.description: The version of the server, the one the contract's `info.version` gives too.

SettingsChange.description:
The settings to change. A member that is left out stays as it is; one that is `null`
goes back to its default.

oneOf.description: Where a card opens.
How much room the interface gives each thing.

haptics.description: Whether a device that can do so answers touches with a vibration.

oneOf.description: How the hours of a day are written.

language.description:
`auto`, for the language of the browser, or a language tag such as `ko` or
`en-US`, in the shape the browsers' `Intl` reads (Unicode BCP 47), at most 64
characters; the server keeps no list of languages, and keeps a tag as given.

oneOf.description: The colors of the interface.

timeZone.description:
`auto`, for the time zone of the device, or the IANA name of a time zone, such
as `Asia/Seoul`.

oneOf.description: The day a week starts on.

Sharing.description:
The sharing state of a board.

The JSON form is what is answered to those who may share the board: whether it is
shared, the read token while it is, and when the state last changed. A board that
was never shared is `{"enabled": false}`.

token.description:
The read token: whoever has it reads the board. The server makes it. Empty, and
left out of the JSON form, while the board is not shared.

updateAt.description:
When the state last changed, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch. Zero, and
left out of the JSON form, for a board that was never shared.

SharingRequest.description: Whether a board is to be shared.

enabled.description:
`true` shares the board, `false` stops sharing it. The read token a board had
stops working when sharing stops.

regenerate.description:
With `enabled`, `true` gives the board a new read token; the old one stops
working.

SnippetPart.description: A stretch of a snippet: text as it is in the body, never markup.

matched.description: Whether the stretch is what the search matched.

SubscriberType.description: The kind of entity that subscribes.

Subscription.description: A subscription to the changes of a board or card.

blockId.description: The identifier of the block subscribed to.

blockType.description: The type of the block subscribed to.

createAt.description: Creation time in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

deleteAt.description: Deletion time in milliseconds since the Unix epoch; zero if not deleted.

notifiedAt.description:
The time of the last notification sent for this subscription, in milliseconds
since the Unix epoch.

subscriberType.description: The kind of entity that subscribes.

Team.description: A named group of people within a workspace.

members.description: Its people, ordered by user identifier.

name.description: Its name, unique within the workspace in any letter case.

TeamMember.description: A person in a team. Neither email addresses nor credentials are exposed.

displayName.description: Their displayed name, empty when none is set.

TeamName.description: The name when creating or renaming a team.

name.description:
The name, by the rule of an organization's: surrounding whitespace is removed, and
what is left is 1 to 64 characters (UTF-16 code units), none of them a control
character or one that shows nothing, breaks a line or turns the text around.

Title.description: A title written before a person's name.

UnlinkRequest.description: A request to remove an identity from the account of the session.

expiresAt.description:
When the upload ends, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch: 24 hours after it was
opened. An upload that has ended is 404, and is thrown away with its parts.

partCount.description: How many parts the file comes in, numbered from 1: none for an empty file.

partSize.description: The size of every part but the last, which has the rest.

uploadId.description:
What the other operations of the upload take. Only the user who opened it may
use it.

UploadState.description: An upload that is open, with what it has received.

containerId.description: The board the file is for; empty for an archive.

expiresAt.description: When the upload ends, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

partCount.description: How many parts the file comes in.

partSize.description: The size of every part but the last.

parts.description: The parts received, by number. A part sent again replaces the one received.

allOf.description:
What the upload is for: `file`, a file of a board (`completeUpload`), or
`import`, an archive to import into a workspace (`importArchive`).

size.description: The size of the file in bytes.

workspaceId.description: The workspace the archive is for; empty for a file.

UploadedFile.description: What an upload answers: the name the file is asked for by.

fileId.description:
The identifier of the file: what `getFile` and `getFileInfo` take, and what an
attachment block, an image or a file block of a body names in its `fileId`.

allOf.description:
The parts of the user's name, which of them the user is shown by, and their
title and credentials. Whoever sees the user's name sees these.

createAt.description:
Creation time in milliseconds since the Unix epoch; zero for a deleted account
(an empty `username`).

deleteAt.description:
When the account was put out of use (deactivated, or its deletion asked), in
milliseconds since the Unix epoch; zero for one in use, and for a deleted account,
which an empty `username` tells.

displayName.description:
The name the user is shown by, by the rule of `PersonName::shown`: empty when
that is the login name, which is shown then. Kept with the account and made anew
whenever its name changes; what a request says of it is not taken over. At most
129 UTF-16 code units (a name's two parts and a space), not unique.

isAdmin.description:
Whether the user is an administrator of the instance. Decided by the server;
nothing a request says about it is taken over.

updateAt.description:
Last modification time in milliseconds since the Unix epoch; zero for a deleted
account.

User.description:
A user account.

The JSON form carries only the public members. The email address, password hash and
the other authentication members are never serialized and are ignored when decoding.

UserIds.description: The identifiers of the users asked for: at least one, at most 200.

UserPreferencesPatch.description:
A change to the bag of state a client keeps with the account: entries the server
stores without knowing what they mean.

UserSettings.description:
The settings of a user. Every member has a value: what was never set, or was reset,
is at its default.

density.description: How much room the interface gives each thing.

haptics.description: Whether a device that can do so answers touches with a vibration.

hourCycle.description: How the hours of a day are written.

language.description:
The language of the interface: `auto` for the browser's, or a language tag such
as `ko` or `en-US`, in the shape the browsers' `Intl` reads (Unicode BCP 47), at
most 64 characters. The server keeps no list of languages, and answers a tag as
it was given, case and all: compare tags without regard to case.

timeZone.description: The time zone times are shown in.

weekStart.description: The day a week starts on.

UserWorkspace.description: A workspace as one of its members finds it among theirs.

name.description: The workspace's name; empty if it was given none.

orgId.description: The identifier of the organization the workspace belongs to.

role.description: What the user is in the workspace.

ssoRequired.description:
Whether the workspace is closed to the session that asks: its organization
takes only sessions made through its provider, and this one was not. What is
under the workspace then answers 401 with the reason `sso_required`; signing in
through the provider of `orgId` opens it.

WeekStart.description: The day a week starts on.

WelcomeBoard.description: What asking for a first board answers: where it is.

boardId.description: The identifier of the new board.

info.description:
The API of an fvoci server.

## Signing in

`login` answers with a `Set-Cookie` header that carries the session: the cookie `__Host-fvoci_session` where the server is reached over HTTPS, `fvoci_session` over plain HTTP. It is `HttpOnly`, so a page's scripts never see it, and a browser sends it by itself. A client that is no browser may send the cookie's value as `Authorization: Bearer <value>` instead. The operations under `/shared/{containerId}` need no session: they read a shared board with its `readToken`, and look at no session that comes along.

## Requests that change something

Every request whose method is not `GET`, `HEAD` or `OPTIONS` needs the header `X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest`, unless it has a bearer token, and is refused with 403 and the reason `csrf` without it. If it has an `Origin` header, the origin must be the server's own (or one the server was configured to accept); otherwise it is refused with 403 and the reason `foreign_origin`.

A page should make these requests with `fetch` in its default mode, `cors`. The server sends its pages with `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, and under that policy a browser writes `Origin: null` on a changing request of any other mode (`same-origin`, `no-cors`, or a form the browser posts itself), which is refused as a foreign origin.

## Answers

An operation answers 200 with a body, 201 with what it made, or 204 with no body. Every other status comes with a `Problem`, the problem details of RFC 9457, as `application/problem+json`: `type` names the kind of the problem and is the same for every problem of the kind, `title` is its name, `status` repeats the status and `detail` says what went wrong this time. `type` is `/problems/<name>` under the path the server is served at, the address of a page of text about the kind; `/problems` lists them, and so does `x-problem-types` of the schema `Problem`, as they are on a server at the root of its host (a server under a path has that path before each). `reason` tells apart causes a client must tell apart; a problem with a `reason` has the `type` of that name, written with hyphens, and any other the `type` of its status. `errors` lists what of the request was refused, each by a JSON Pointer into the body (`pointer`), the name of a parameter of the query or the path (`parameter`), or the name of a header (`header`). `limit` is the limit that was exceeded: bytes for a body that was too large (413), a count for too many of something. `instance` is the request, `urn:uuid:` and its `requestId`. A session that is missing or over is 401. What the user may not see is 404, as if it were not there; what they may see but not do is 403. A path that is no operation is 404 too, and a method an operation's path does not have is 405.

A request without a session whose JSON body has more than 64 KiB is 413 before it is 401. A body larger than its route reads is 413 with the reason `request_too_large` and the `limit` in bytes.

Any request may be answered 503 with the reason `database_busy`: the database did not take one of its statements in time (another write held the file, or no connection to it was to be had). That statement did nothing and may be taken a moment later. A request of one step may be sent again as it is; of one of several (`completeUpload`, `importArchive`) what was done before stays done, and sent again it is answered as its operation says.

The identifiers of users, workspaces, boards, blocks and categories are UUIDs, written lower-case with hyphens; a client takes every identifier as an opaque string. A `fileId` is no UUID: it is an unguessable name that ends in the file's extension. Times are milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

## Lists

Every list comes in an order, and the description of each operation says which. Where it says nothing else, the order is that of creation, oldest first, and by identifier among what was created in the same millisecond.

## Bodies edited together

While people edit a card's body together the server holds it as a Y document. What it refuses of an editor has the reason `update_refused`, `update_out_of_step`, `update_too_large` or `document_too_large`; `too_many_documents` and `document_unavailable` say that it cannot take the document for now. A write of a card's whole body here (a patch of the card or of blocks, a card stored again) first writes to the card what its editors typed: a `readAt` from before that is refused with 409, and if it cannot be written the write is refused with `document_unavailable`. The editors themselves speak to the server over the websocket, whose messages name the same reasons (`contracts/websocket.md`); `document_read_only`, `connection_too_slow`, `too_many_documents_joined`, `document_full`, `too_many_connections_joined` and `too_many_frames` come only there. The page of each kind says when it comes. `search_not_configured` comes from none of these operations: only from the reindex of the administration socket, on a server configured without a search server (a search there searches its database).

## Request bodies

A request schema lists the members a request is for. A member that is not required may be left out. `null` is a value only of a member whose schema allows it, and is then none; `null` for any other member is refused with 400, as a value of another type is. A member the schema marks as required is one the request cannot do without; where the server takes a missing one as empty instead of refusing the request, the result is that of the empty value (a login without a password is a failed login). A body with members the schema does not list is mostly not refused for them. The exceptions: `patchUserSettings` and `patchMe` refuse every member they do not know, `createBoard` and `createCategory` refuse an `id`, and `setSharing` refuses a `token`.

get.description:
Where a provider sends the browser back to: each organization has an address of its
own, its provider's `redirectUri`, and a sign-in started for one organization does
not finish at another's address, nor with an `iss` (RFC 9207) other than the
provider's, before any code is exchanged. The sign-in is taken by its `state`, once, and only from the
browser that started it; another browser takes nothing. The code is
exchanged for an ID token, whose signature, issuer, audience, time and nonce are
checked. The person is known by the issuer and the subject: an account of theirs
signs in, and somebody who has none gets one, if the organization lets newcomers in
and no account has their email address. A registration that waits for that address
to be confirmed (`register`, `acceptInvitation`) stands in nobody's way. Where the
provider vouches for the address, one made by a link of this organization is
removed with the sign-in, new account or known: the use it took of the link is
given back, and the link mailed for it confirms nothing any more. A registration
of its own, or by a link of another organization, stays, and so does any at a
trial of pending settings and at a sign-in that carries over. The session comes in the `Set-Cookie`
header, and the browser goes to the web app (303). A sign-in that was started to
link sets no session: the browser goes to the web app with `oidc_linked=1` in the
query. A trial of the provider's pending settings (`startOidcTrial`) that ends well
makes them the provider's and sets the session, made through them, and the browser
goes to the organization's page (`/org/{orgId}`) with `oidc_pending=applied`; one
that fails changes nothing, and goes there with `oidc_pending_error` naming the
reason as `oidc_error` does (among them `oidc_trial_account` and
`oidc_trial_stale`).

Otherwise the browser goes to the login page of the organization (`/login?org=…`),
with the reason of what went wrong in `oidc_error`, by the name of its problem
(`oidc_state_invalid` as `oidc-state-invalid`): `oidc_state_invalid`, `oidc_denied`,
`oidc_token_refused`, `oidc_token_invalid`, `oidc_email_missing`,
`oidc_email_unverified`, `oidc_email_taken`, `oidc_join_closed`,
`oidc_identity_taken`, `oidc_email_mismatch`, `oidc_carry_over_refused` or
`oidc_unavailable`.

While the organization keeps the provider it moved away from (`former` of its
provider), a sign-in that vouches for somebody who has no account makes none: what
the provider said is held for this browser for ten minutes, under a cookie of its
own, and the browser goes to the login page with `oidc_held=1`, which asks whether
the person had an account: `startOidcCarryOver` if they had, `finishHeldOidcLogin`
if not. A sign-in through the former provider, which `startOidcCarryOver` starts,
comes back here too: it sets a session only by carrying the held sign-in over.
Where nothing is carried over it goes to the login page with
`oidc_carry_over_refused`, and where the sign-in itself failed (refused by the
former provider, its token not taken, not this browser's) with that reason, as
any sign-in does. An account that comes into the organization by the sign-in, as a
member, is given its welcome board unless it has one (`onboard` says more): in the
language of its settings, or else in the one `Accept-Language` prefers.

post.description:
For the login page of the server, as a request of its own, not an address a browser
is sent to: like every request that changes something it needs the header
`X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest` and no foreign `Origin`, which a page of another
site cannot send, so that no such page can sign a browser in to an account of its
choosing. Starts a sign-in for the organization `org` and answers where the page
sends the browser (the provider), with a cookie that ties the sign-in to this
browser, and ten minutes to come back. 409 with the reason `oidc_unavailable` if
the organization has no provider that is on, or it cannot be reached; 429 when
this address made too many sign-ins of late.

With `linkPassword` in the body the sign-in links: it needs the session of the
browser's cookie (401 without; a bearer token does not do, as the browser comes back
with its cookie), whose account's password that is, and when the browser comes back, who the provider
vouches for is tied to that account in place of signing in (`getMyIdentities`);
after that the provider signs in to the account. No account is made and none is
joined to another: an identity that is another account's is refused
(`oidc_identity_taken`), and so is one whose email address, as the provider has
checked it, is not the account's own (`oidc_email_mismatch`): the password ties no
other person of the provider to the account. It ends only in the browser that started it and still has
the session it was started from (`oidc_state_invalid` otherwise). A wrong password
is 400 with the reason `invalid_credentials`, naming `/linkPassword`, counted as a
wrong one of `changePassword` is; an account without a password is 409 with the
reason `password_not_set`. The session need not open the organization. A body with
another member, or a `linkPassword` that is no text, is 400 naming it: what was
meant to link does not sign in instead.

post.description:
Consumes the token of the link mailed to a registration's address, within a day of
the mail and seven days of the registration: makes the account, and the
organization and first workspace it registered with, and signs it in. The session
comes in the `Set-Cookie` header, as from `login`, and the answer says where the
account was let in. A link is used once, and a newer mail of the same registration
ends the links before it. A missing, ended, used or replaced token answers 400,
naming `token` in `errors`.

Only who registered finishes a registration, so that nobody is signed in to an
account whose password somebody else chose. In the browser the registration was
made from, which the cookie of `register` or `acceptInvitation` shows, the token is
enough. Anywhere else a token that would confirm is answered 403 with the reason
`password_required`, and the request is sent again with `password`, the password the
registration was made with: a wrong one is the 401 of `login` (`invalid_credentials`),
counted with the failed logins to the registration's user name, and too many are
429. A request that is refused so leaves the link as it was. Nothing is asked of a
token that confirms nothing, so the answers tell no more of whether a registration
waits than the token does.

On a server that takes one organization and has its first user by now,
the registration is removed and the answer is 403 with the reason
`invitation_required`. A registration made by the link of an invitation
(`acceptInvitation`) is let in as the acceptance would have let it in, and the answer
names the board of a guest's link (`containerId`); if the link lets nobody in any more
(revoked, or who made it may no longer invite), the registration is removed and the
answer is 404 with the reason `invitation_unavailable`. Requests are counted by where they come from, as
registrations are, and too many are 429.

An account that a link for members lets in so is given its welcome board in the
workspace, unless it has one (`onboard` says more): written in the `language` of
the acceptance if that was English or Korean, or else in English.

post.description:
Lets somebody into the workspace the link of `token` leads into, and answers where
that is. A request with a session lets in the user of the session, and names no
`account` (400 if it does). A request without one makes the `account` it names and
lets that in: the account's members are checked as `register` checks them (400,
with `errors`, which name them under `/account`), and a name or an email address
that is taken is 409 with the reason `username_taken` or `email_taken`. Accepting
does not sign in.

A member's link makes the account a member of the workspace and of its
organization; who is a guest of the workspace becomes a member, and who works there
already stays what they are. A guest's link puts the account on its board, in the
link's role or the higher one the account has there: who is no member of the
workspace becomes a guest of it (and no member of its organization), and who is one
stays what they are in it. The answer names the board then (`containerId`). The account
is made, the membership stored and the use of the link counted together or not at
all, and an acceptance that changes nothing uses nothing of the link.

On a server that asks for the email address of a registration to be confirmed
(`emailVerification` of `getLoginOptions`), a new `account` waits for its address,
unless the link was made for one recipient of a mailed guest link at that address,
which the mail proves: the answer is 202 with no body, nobody is let in, and the
link mailed to the address (`completeEmailVerification`) makes the account and lets
it in, as this acceptance would have, and signs it in. The 202 sets the cookie of
the browser the registration was made from, as `register` does. The registration counts as a
use of the link from the start, so a link for one guest lets nobody else in
meanwhile, and it holds its name and address as an account would. Not confirmed in
seven days, it is removed and gives the use back. A new `account` from the browser
of a registration that waits still (by this link, another, or `register`) replaces
that registration: its name and address are free for the account, and the use it
took of a link is given back, so that a link for one guest takes the same person
again with the address put right. `language` is the language of the
mail (English or Korean).

A session that the link's organization does not take (it takes no password,
`ssoRequired`, and the session was not made through its provider) is 401 with the
reason `sso_required` and its `orgId`, and lets nobody in.

A token that lets nobody in is 404 with the reason `invitation_unavailable`,
whatever is wrong with it: there is no such link, it ended, it was used as often as
it may be, it was revoked, or who made it may no longer invite. Requests are counted
by where they come from, and too many are 429.

An account that a link for members lets in is given its welcome board in the
workspace, a private board of its own, unless it has one (`onboard` says more):
written in the language of the account's settings, or else in `language` for an
account made here, if that is English or Korean, or else in the one
`Accept-Language` prefers. An account whose address is confirmed first is given
it then (`completeEmailVerification`).
