Sets the organization's `OpenID Connect` provider, in place of the one it has. The
discovery document of an issuer that is not the organization's already is read
first: it must name the issuer exactly and have
`https` endpoints, or the request is 400 with the reason `oidc_issuer_unverified`
and `errors` naming `/issuer`. The server reaches only `https` addresses, follows no
redirect, and reaches only public addresses unless its configuration lets it
(`oidc_allow_private_addresses`).

`clientSecret` left out keeps the stored secret while the issuer and the client stay
the same; with another issuer or client it is required when a secret is stored (400,
`required` at `/clientSecret`), as the secret is the old client's. The empty string
stores none. The secret is stored sealed with the server's key and never answered:
without the key the request is 409 with the reason `secret_key_required`. `autoJoin`
and `enabled` left out stay as they are, also for another issuer or client, and are
on when the organization has no provider.

While the organization takes no password and the request keeps it so, another
issuer, client or secret is not taken at once: it is saved aside as the provider's
`pending` settings (in place of pending ones there are), and people go on signing
in through the provider as it is. A sign-in through the pending settings
(`startOidcTrial`) that ends well makes them the provider's; `deleteOidcPending`
throws them away. The secret of the pending settings is never answered either. What
else the request changes (`autoJoin`) is taken at once; `enabled` false is refused
(`sso_enforced`). While the organization takes a password a change is taken at
once, and a change of what signing in takes throws pending settings away.

on, what is the organization's (the routes under `/w/{workspaceId}` and
`/org/{orgId}`, and `setUserAdmin` where the organization is the instance's own, the
oldest) answers 401 with the reason `sso_required` to every session that was not
made through this provider, `getMyMemberships` leaves its boards out for one, and
the websocket follows none of its workspaces for one. The sessions stay, and open
what is of other organizations. It is switched on by a
session that was itself made through this provider, switched on, as it is stored
(`canRequireSso`), by a request that does not change its issuer, client, secret or
`enabled`, or the request is 409 with the reason `sso_unproven`: who asks has then
shown that it lets them in. A `clientSecret` sent as it is stored is no change.
While it is on, the provider is not switched off (`enabled` false) and not removed:
409 with the reason `sso_enforced`, unless the same request switches `ssoRequired`
off. Left out it stays as it is,
and is off when the organization has no provider. A provider changed by another request
since this one read it is 409, to be read and sent again. The answer's `redirectUri`
is the address to register with the provider, exactly: the organization's own,
`…/api/v1/auth/oidc/callback/{orgId}`, the same before the provider is set and after
it is changed.

post.description:
Makes an account and the organization it starts: `organizationName` names the
organization and its first workspace, and the account administers both. On a server that takes one organization (`org_creation` is `first_user_only`)
only the first user registers, and administers the server too; everybody after is
refused with 403 and the reason `invitation_required`, whatever else the request
says, and gets in by the link of an invitation (`acceptInvitation`). A name or an
email address that is taken is 409 with the reason `username_taken` or
`email_taken`. Registering does not sign in.

On a server that asks for the email address to be confirmed (`emailVerification` of
`getLoginOptions`), registering makes no account: it answers 202 with no body, and
mails a link to the address, in the language of `language` (English or Korean), that
makes the account and the organization and signs in (`completeEmailVerification`).
Until then there is nothing of it but its name and address, which are taken as an
account's are, for seven days; a registration that is not confirmed by then is
removed, and its name and address are free again. The 202 sets a cookie that tells
the browser the registration was made from (`fvoci_signup`, `__Host-fvoci_signup`
over HTTPS; `HttpOnly`, for the seven days): no session, it reaches nothing, and
shows `completeEmailVerification` that the browser is the registrant's. A
registration from a browser that has the cookie of one that waits still replaces
that one: whoever mistyped an address registers again at once, under the same user
name, and the link mailed for the first confirms nothing any more. Without the
cookie the name and the address of a registration that waits are taken.

The name and the email address must not be blank, the email address must look like
one, the display name (`displayName`, may be left out) is checked as `patchMe` checks it,
the password must have at least 8 characters and at most 1024 bytes, and the organization
name must not be blank, and is otherwise read as a display name is; otherwise the
request is 400, and `errors` names every member that is refused, each with
its `reason`: `required`, `invalid_format`, `too_short`, `too_long` or
`invalid_characters`.

post.description:
Puts the account of the session out of use, to be erased after thirty days
(`graceDays` of `getAccountDeletion`): every session of it ends, this one too, and
its cookie is cleared. Until it is erased, whoever signs in to the account gets a
session that opens nothing (every operation is 401 with the reason
`account_deletion_pending`) but `getAccountDeletion`, `cancelAccountDeletion` and
`logout`. While it waits, the account stays a member of what it is a member of,
shown as one, and what it wrote stays; the links of invitations it made let nobody
in, and it may wait past the thirty days until it is erased.

Erased, the account is gone from every organization, workspace, board and wiki; a
board it alone administered passes to an administrator of its workspace; nothing of
the person is kept, and what it wrote stays under its identifier, which
`getWorkspaceUsersById` answers with no name: the writer is a deleted user. An
organization that has nobody else goes with it, but the server's own first one,
whose only administrator stays as the only one of an organization with other
people does.

`username` is the account's login name, in any letter case: another is 400 naming
`/username`. An account with a password (`proof` is `password`) sends it: a wrong
one is 400 with the reason `invalid_credentials`, naming `/password`, and too many
are 429, as for `changePassword`. An account without one (`proof` is `sign_in`)
asks from a session made through a provider no more than five minutes ago:
otherwise 403 with the reason `sign_in_again`.

An organization that would go with the account and that takes only sessions made
through its provider is asked of such a session: any other is 401 with the reason
`sso_required` and its `orgId`. Leaving an organization is the account's own, and
asked of any session.

The server's only administrator stays (409, reason `last_admin`), and so does the
only administrator of an organization that stays when the account goes: one that
has other people in it, or the server's own first organization (409, reason
`last_org_admin`, `orgId` naming the first such organization): make somebody else
an administrator first.
